answer: Registration is one shared inlet. A new identity enters a single throttled gate metered by origin, not by wallet, so a batch of names presses the same pipe and each waits longer than the last. Credit should ripple back to whoever paid that queue: a second history signed in one epoch damps the emission of every identity sharing that inlet, and lifts only after a season of divergent, attested work. To forge a usable record an identity must burn measured effort at the gate, carrying proof forward instead of declaring it. The ripple lands on the backers who vouched.
